neighbours.label: ' around' / ' front' placing one thing in a fixed position relative to another (paint dabbed around the edges, a cup set in front of someone), not ' around' as a path of motion or as 'approximately'
fire: He wrapped a thick bandage around the dog's injured paw.
She tied a red ribbon around the neck of the bottle.
The gardener spread fresh mulch around the base of each rose.
They built a low stone wall around the vegetable plot.
The waiter set a bowl of soup in front of the old man.
He parked the wheelbarrow in front of the shed door.
She smeared a ring of glue around the rim of the jar.
The nurse fastened the cuff around the patient's upper arm.
quiet: He ran around the park twice before breakfast.
She arrived around noon with a bottle of wine.
The gardener wandered around the town looking for roses.
They drove around the island in about two hours.
The waiter came back around nine with the soup.
He turned around and stared at the shed door.
She has been around horses since she was a child.
The nurse said it would take around ten minutes.

notes: Card: ' around' x6, ' at', ' front', ' pattern', ' representing', ' corresponding'. Probe: dabbed paint around 0.99, strapped around 0.85, in front of 0.93, beside 0.50; walked around the lake 0.03, around three o'clock 0.04. Also fires on ' pattern' (1.25), ' representing' (0.80), ' corresponding' (0.68), which this test does not cover; the wider reading may be 'one thing standing in a fixed relation to another'.
